name: Trochanteric osteotomy for hip exposure (periprosthetic)
corridor: Osteotomy of the greater trochanter with the abductors attached, mobilized to widen exposure of the hip and acetabulum, then reattached with cables or a claw plate

positioning.text: Position in lateral decubitus through a posterolateral approach that can extend into a Kocher-Langenbeck exposure.

surface_landmarks.text: Mark the tip of the greater trochanter and the vastus tubercle.

incision.text: Use the posterolateral skin incision, incising the vastus lateralis fascia distally 5 to 8 cm for extraperiosteal mobilization.

superficial_interval.text: Cauterize the trochanteric anastomotic vessels, then make the osteotomy from the tip of the trochanter to the base of the vastus tubercle with a cooled saw or osteotome.

deep_interval.text: Mobilize the trochanteric fragment with its attached abductors, releasing gluteus minimus from the retroacetabular surface and femoral insertion, keeping the vastus lateralis in continuity.

layers.text: Skin, subcutaneous tissue, fascia lata, the trochanteric fragment with abductors, and the hip capsule.

structures_at_risk.text: The sciatic nerve posteriorly and the medial femoral circumflex artery supplying the head are at risk, and the short external rotators should be tagged for repair.

danger_zones.text: The retroacetabular surface where the sciatic nerve lies is the danger zone; the trochanteric anastomosis should be cauterized before the cut to protect the head blood supply.

retraction_hazards.text: Palpate and protect the sciatic nerve and avoid over-retraction of the mobilized abductor fragment.

exposure.text: Widely exposes the hip and acetabulum for revision arthroplasty or periprosthetic fracture fixation.

limitations.text: Active abduction must be limited postoperatively to prevent osteotomy escape, and nonunion of the trochanter can occur.

indications.text: Indicated for revision hip arthroplasty and ORIF of periprosthetic acetabular and femoral fractures requiring wide exposure.

closure.text: Reattach the trochanter with cerclage wires through drill holes or a trochanteric claw or hook plate, repair the capsule and rotators, and close in layers.

complications.text: Complications include trochanteric nonunion or escape, sciatic nerve injury, and abductor weakness.

procedure_applications.condition: Wider access to the hip or acetabulum is needed during periprosthetic fracture fixation
Improved acetabular and proximal femoral exposure is required for revision

questions.question: Between which points does the standard trochanteric osteotomy run?
questions.answer: From the tip of the greater trochanter to the base of the vastus tubercle.

questions.question: What must be limited postoperatively to protect the osteotomy?
questions.answer: Active abduction, to prevent osteotomy escape.

questions.question: How is the trochanter reattached?
questions.answer: With cerclage wires through drill holes or a trochanteric claw/hook plate.
